stories.headline: Nvidia faces China export restrictions and CEO return debate
stories.dek: Nvidia is navigating export controls and shareholder calls for former CEO Jensen Huang's return.
points: Nvidia is halting H200 chip sales in China due to export restrictions [1]
Shareholders are pushing for a special committee to decide on Jensen Huang's return [2]
There are new claims against Jensen Huang involving threats and sexual remarks [3]
stories.why: The controversy highlights the intersection of geopolitics and business, with export controls affecting revenue and leadership decisions impacting stock performance. Companies and investors must navigate these complex dynamics.

timeline.what: Nvidia announced it would no longer sell H200 chips in China [1]
A shareholder wrote an open letter calling for a special committee to decide on Jensen Huang's return [2]
New claims surfaced against Jensen Huang involving threats and sexual remarks [3]

stories.eli5: Nvidia is having problems with selling chips to China and some people want the old boss back. There are also new stories about the old boss that are making people worried.

voices.said: Nvidia is shutting down chip sales in China due to export restrictions [1]
The board should decide on Jensen Huang's return through a special committee [2]
The company is yet to confirm or dismiss old claims against the ex CEO [3]

unclear: Whether the new claims against Jensen Huang are true
The exact impact of export restrictions on Nvidia's revenue
Whether the board will create a special committee for the CEO decision

stories.headline: Amazon seeks $7.5 billion Decart deal to boost AI chip efficiency
stories.dek: Amazon is close to acquiring Decart for $7.5 billion to enhance AI chip efficiency and compete with Nvidia.
points: Amazon is nearing a $7.5 billion deal to acquire Decart, as reported by the Financial Times [1]
Decart's software improves AI model efficiency, freeing up computer chip capacity [1]
Decart was valued at $4 billion in May after raising $300 million in funding [1]
stories.why: The acquisition could help Amazon strengthen its position in the AI chip market against Nvidia, impacting both tech and investment strategies. It reflects the growing importance of AI efficiency in the tech industry.

timeline.what: Decart raised $300 million in funding, reaching a $4 billion valuation [1]
Anthropic explored a potential $6 billion deal with Decart [1]
Amazon is close to finalizing the $7.5 billion acquisition of Decart [1]

stories.eli5: Amazon wants to buy a company called Decart to make their AI chips work better, so they can compete with another big tech company called Nvidia.

voices.said: As AI reshapes investing behaviour, capital is increasingly flowing into decentralized ecosystems, redefining how assets are managed.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO challenges Wall Street norms
stories.dek: Anthropic's IPO process faced unique challenges and restrictions from the company.
points: Anthropic instructed some underwriters to limit deal teams to four bankers [1]
Banks received last-minute changes to the S-1A filing [1]
Anthropic asked bank officers to sign non-competes covering rivals [1]
stories.why: The unique IPO process highlights the growing power of tech companies over Wall Street, which could reshape how startups raise funds. This shift could benefit tech firms but challenge traditional banking practices.

timeline.what: Reuters reported on Anthropic's IPO challenges
Corrected S-1A filing was sent to banks

stories.eli5: A big tech company called Anthropic made it hard for Wall Street bankers to do their job when they went public, causing some problems and complaints.

voices.said: Tech companies have market power to change how IPOs work

stories.headline: Tata Sons faces governance clash over listing and control
stories.dek: Tata Trusts and directors clash over whether Tata Sons should list and who should lead.
points: Tata Sons board meeting this week will revisit listing issues amid a governance dispute [1]
Trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh have challenged Noel Tata on governance matters [1]
Noel Tata's letter to the Tata Trusts questioned communication with the RBI on listing [2]
stories.why: The dispute affects governance and control of a major Indian business empire, impacting its ability to raise capital and operate smoothly. The outcome could influence how Tata Sons navigates regulatory and financial challenges.

timeline.what: Tata Sons directors overruled opposition from Noel Tata on listing efforts and reappointment of Chandrasekaran
Noel Tata sent a letter challenging the minutes of the Sep 17 meeting and raised conflict-of-interest concerns

stories.eli5: Big bosses at Tata are arguing about whether to let the company go public and who should lead. This could affect how the company makes money and runs its business.

stories.headline: Reliance Brands reports revenue growth and reduced loss in FY26
stories.dek: Reliance Brands saw a 3.8% revenue increase and narrowed its loss in FY26.
points: Reliance Brands revenue rose 3.77% to Rs 3,390.89 crore in FY26 [1]
The company's loss narrowed to Rs 137.04 crore from Rs 233.79 crore in FY25 [1]
RBL expanded its portfolio with new global brand partnerships in FY26 [1]
stories.why: The reduced loss shows improved financial performance, which is important for investors and business partners. The expansion into premium fashion segments may increase market share and revenue potential.

timeline.what: RBL operated 1,085 Points of Sale across India
RBL added three globally recognised brands through master franchise partnerships
RBL reported revenue from operations of Rs 3,267.66 crore and a profit of Rs 237.12 crore

stories.eli5: Reliance Brands made more money this year than last, and they lost less money, which is good news for their business.

voices.said: The company achieved a net turnover of Rs 3,390.89 crore as compared to Rs 3,267.66 crore during last year
The company registered a loss of Rs 137.13 crore as compared to Rs 233.79 crore during last year

unclear: The exact impact of new brand partnerships on future revenue is unclear

stories.headline: Indian startups see record IPO success in 2025
stories.dek: Indian startups raised over ₹41,248 Cr in 2025 through IPOs.
points: Eighteen Indian startups listed on the bourses in 2025, raising ₹41,248 Cr [1]
SEBI reforms and simplified DRHP filings helped reduce red tape [1]
Retail investors and OFS component provided liquidity to early backers [1]
stories.why: Investors are prioritizing profitability and sustainable growth over hype, which benefits well-governed tech companies. Founders who focus on long-term value creation are rewarded by public markets.

timeline.what: 18 startups listed on the bourses, raising ₹41,240 Cr
17 new-age tech companies made their D-Street debut
Unicorns like OYO and Razorpay could raise nearly ₹20,000 Cr

voices.said: Founders who plan to grow their businesses over decades are rewarded by public markets

stories.headline: Gold prices fall to 14-month low amid AI selloff and Fed rate concerns
stories.dek: Gold prices have dropped to a 14-month low as market forces shift.
points: Gold prices have fallen to a 14-month low as investors sell due to concerns over AI spending and potential Fed rate hikes [2]
Gold's five-year winning streak is under threat after a dramatic selloff, with prices now near $3,510 per ounce [1]
Silver has also crashed, reaching its lowest level since September 2025, alongside platinum and other metals [2]
stories.why: AI spending slowdowns and Fed rate hike expectations are affecting investor sentiment, which can impact tech and finance sectors. Gold and silver are seen as safe-haven assets, so their decline may signal broader economic uncertainty.

timeline.what: Gold reached a record high of $5,594.82 per ounce [1]
Gold prices began to fall as the US dollar strengthened and risk appetite improved [1]
Gold prices have fallen to a 14-month low, with silver also crashing to its lowest level since September 2025 [2]

stories.eli5: Gold is losing value because people are worried about the economy and the US might raise interest rates. This makes gold less attractive, so its price drops.

voices.said: Silver has more systematic demand due to its use in EVs and electronics, unlike gold [2]

stories.headline: InvIT IPOs to raise Rs 17,000 crore by March 2027
stories.dek: India's InvIT market sees growing interest as more trusts plan public offerings.
points: Four to five InvITs plan to go public by March 2027, raising Rs 17,000 crore [1]
InvITs have already raised Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25 [1]
Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust filed for a Rs 6,000-crore IPO [1]
NHAI-sponsored Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust raised Rs 6,000 crore in March [1]
stories.why: The expansion of InvITs provides a stable income stream for investors, and the increased capital can support tech and infrastructure projects. This is particularly relevant for tech and business professionals looking to invest in long-term, income-generating assets.
